headline: The main drug used
body: has a side effect list nobody measures in the people taking it for height.
punch: Not because it's safe. Because nobody checked.

headline: Aromatase inhibitors
body: Letrozole and anastrozole block testosterone converting into estrogen. Less estrogen means slower bone maturation, and in boys that means more adult height.
punch: That part is well documented. The monitoring isn't.

headline: The same drugs
body: In postmenopausal breast cancer, aromatase inhibitors are standard therapy, often for years. That population has been studied hard for adverse effects.
punch: Which means we know exactly what to look for.

headline: And there
body: Joint and muscle pain. Altered retinal function. Subtle hits to verbal and visual memory in some patients. Your brain makes its own estrogen and these drugs block that too.
punch: The brain isn't collateral. It's an aromatase expressing organ.

headline: Now the gap
body: Paediatric height studies of these drugs generally don't screen for the sensory or cognitive outcomes oncology treats as standard safety monitoring.
punch: A median 25 months of treatment with zero cognitive endpoints recorded.

headline: There is one reassurance
body: A single line in the literature says letrozole doesn't impair cognitive development in boys. That's one citation, not a monitoring programme.
punch: One reassuring sentence is not the same as having measured it.

headline: It might genuinely be fine
body: A developing brain might compensate differently than an ageing one. That's a decent explanation for why the oncology findings might not transfer.
punch: Decent explanation. Completely untested in this group.

headline: So the honest position
body: Effective for height in the right clinical setting, under supervision, and carrying a documented adverse effect profile that the height literature never went looking for.
punch: No reported harm isn't evidence of no harm when nobody measured.

headline: It's never over
body: Real mechanisms, real citations, no protocols.
